tool.name: ChIP-R
tool.command: #if len($peaks) < 2 echo 'ChIP-R requires at least two replicate peak files in this wrapper.' >&2; exit 1; #elif int($minentries) > len($peaks) echo 'Minimum overlapping replicates must not exceed the number of input files.' >&2; exit 1; #else chipr --input #for $peak in $peaks '$peak' #end for --output chipr --minentries $minentries --rankmethod '$advanced.rankmethod' --duphandling '$advanced.duphandling' --seed $advanced.seed --size $advanced.size $advanced.fragment > '$execution_log' 2>&1 #end if

param.name: peaks
param.label: Peak files from biological replicates
param.help: Select at least two files on the same genome assembly, one per replicate. BED inputs must contain the 9 broadPeak or 10 narrowPeak columns; BED3/BED6 are not sufficient.

param.label: Minimum number of overlapping replicates
param.help: Must not exceed the number of files. The wrapper defaults to 2; the ChIP-R CLI defaults to 1.

param.label: Rank peaks within each replicate by
Random seed
param.help: Used for random ordering of equal ranks.

param.label: Fallback minimum peak size (bp)
param.help: Used when reconnecting fragments without surrounding peaks; this is not a strict minimum size filter on all output peaks.

tool.help:
ChIP-R assesses peak reproducibility across ChIP-seq or ATAC-seq replicates using rank products, peak fragmentation and a binomial threshold.
Inputs ------ Select at least two narrowPeak or broadPeak files, one per biological replicate, on the same genome assembly. Files labelled BED must still have the complete 9 or 10 peak columns. Use a ranking column that contains meaningful values in every replicate; do not rank by p-value or q-value if that column is missing (-1). ENCODE narrowPeak/broadPeak p-value and q-value fields use -log10 values. This tool starts from called peaks, not BAM or FASTQ files.
Outputs ------- * Optimal peaks: primary peaks selected by the binomial threshold. * All peaks: primary and secondary peaks, sorted by significance. * Peak summary: peak counts and chromosome size statistics. * Execution log: stdout and stderr from ChIP-R.
Both peak tables have 9 columns: chromosome, start, end, name, score, strand, signalValue, pValue and qValue. ChIP-R 1.2.0 writes raw probabilities in the last two columns. Outputs are deliberately typed as tabular: these columns are neither standard BED9 fields nor ENCODE -log10 peak scores. Coordinates retain BED's zero-based, half-open convention.
Version-specific behavior ------------------------- This wrapper targets ChIP-R 1.2.0. Its actual output names are ``prefix_all.bed``, ``prefix_optimal.bed`` and ``prefix_log.txt``, rather than the tier names in the upstream README. The CLI accepts --alpha, but the implementation does not use it to select primary peaks. It is therefore not exposed here. The optimal output uses the binomial threshold, not a user-specified alpha/FDR cutoff.
The wrapper defaults to two overlapping replicates; choose a higher value when a stricter overlap requirement is needed.
